newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific sees growth for US operations.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific sees growth for US operations.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources will continue to grow its domestic operations and is looking at opportunities in broking electricity and wholesaling natural gas, chief operating officer George Lindahl said.

"We have no plans to do high risk exploration and production outside the U.S., we see years and years of opportunities domestically, so it makes sense to stay here," Lindahl said in an interview on Wednesday.
The company said it intends to move further down the supply chain to its customers and diversifying its business.
"We are looking very seriously at extending into broking electricity and wholesaling natural gas right to the city gate so as to extend the profit chain," Lindahl said.

Union Pacific produces 1.8 billion cubic feet of natural gas annually and has the largest domestic capital spending plans for 1997 of any indenpendent energy company and will spend over $1.0 billion this year, mostly in the Austin Chalk area in Texas and in the Rockies.

Lindahl said that Union Pacific had hedged 70 percent of its natural gas output at $2.00 per thousand cubic feet, 15 percent higher than in 1996 and 85 percent of its oil at a level that was 50 cents higher than 1996.

New pipeline capacity for Canadian natural gas coming online later this decade would have little impact on UPR's Rockies production, which could be shipped into the MidWest via the Crazy Horse pipeline.
"Also, we own the leases, whereas most other producers are repaying 20 percent royalties, so we can compete at lower prices," Lindahl noted.
